entries.zh: Let an agent drive a browser: which layer does what
entries.en: Let an agent drive a browser: which layer does what
entries.summaryZh: A browser agent is often sold as one product, but it is four layers: browser runtime (sessions, cookies, proxies), page understanding (DOM / vision / accessibility tree), action execution (click, type, wait) and audit (screenshots, logs, replay). This page maps each layer to an existing entry.
entries.summaryEn: A browser agent is often sold as one product, but it is four layers: browser runtime (sessions, cookies, proxies), page understanding (DOM / vision / accessibility tree), action execution (click, type, wait) and audit (screenshots, logs, replay). This page maps each layer to an existing entry.

entries.zh: Agent memory: what to write, how to read, when to forget
entries.en: Agent memory: what to write, how to read, when to forget
entries.summaryZh: “Having memory” is not storing every chat turn. At minimum, separate working memory (current task), episodic memory (what happened) and semantic memory (stable facts and preferences). Each layer needs write, retrieval, expiry and deletion policies, or memory becomes noise.
entries.summaryEn: “Having memory” is not storing every chat turn. At minimum, separate working memory (current task), episodic memory (what happened) and semantic memory (stable facts and preferences). Each layer needs write, retrieval, expiry and deletion policies, or memory becomes noise.

entries.zh: Realtime voice agents: five latency points on one chain
entries.en: Realtime voice agents: five latency points on one chain
entries.summaryZh: Realtime voice is not “TTS + LLM”: end-to-end latency is the sum of transport, VAD/interruption, STT, LLM first token and TTS first packet. Write a budget for each segment before choosing vendors; otherwise swapping one model still leaves the user feeling half a beat behind.
entries.summaryEn: Realtime voice is not “TTS + LLM”: end-to-end latency is the sum of transport, VAD/interruption, STT, LLM first token and TTS first packet. Write a budget for each segment before choosing vendors; otherwise swapping one model still leaves the user feeling half a beat behind.

entries.summaryZh: IBM’s enterprise-oriented open-weight family: restrained sizes, clean licensing, and an emphasis on workflows and coding, suited to private deployment in compliance-heavy enterprises. It is not a benchmark-maximalist line; its advantage is licensing, auditability and enterprise integration.
entries.summaryEn: IBM’s enterprise-oriented open-weight family: restrained sizes, clean licensing, and an emphasis on workflows and coding, suited to private deployment in compliance-heavy enterprises. It is not a benchmark-maximalist line; its advantage is licensing, auditability and enterprise integration.

entries.summaryZh: Kuaishou Kwaipilot's coding line: the API build stays closed, the Dev build is open-weight. The Kimi chat product sits in the CAC first batch; weights and service filing are separate.

entries.summaryZh: The most permissively licensed coding line (OpenMDW-1.1, fully permissive); its pitch is agentic coding on a local machine, with 3B active parameters as the source of that locality. This site covers Laguna XS-2.1 quantisations.

entries.summaryZh: NVIDIA’s open-weight agent family: three MoE tiers from a single machine to a cluster, pitched at long context, reasoning and local agents. entries.en: Visa TAP: letting merchants recognise trusted shopping agents

entries.zh: x402: paying for APIs over HTTP 402
entries.en: x402: paying for APIs over HTTP 402
entries.summaryZh: The intersection: putting pay-per-call back into HTTP semantics — the server returns 402 plus payment instructions, the client pays, then receives the resource, with no accounts, sessions or credential management. For AI agents this means tool calls can carry their own budget: a paid API call and its payment settle in
